arxiv-2107-06601.title: Well-posedness Properties for a Stochastic Rotating Shallow Water Model
arxiv-2107-06601.creator: Dan Crisan, Oana Lang
arxiv-2107-06601.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the well-posedness properties of a stochastic rotating shallow water system. An inviscid version of this model has first been derived in [ 17 ] and the noise is chosen according to the Stochastic Advection by Lie Transport theory presented in [ 17 ] .

arxiv-2303-07042.title: Harmonic Field-based Provable Exploration of 3D Indoor Environments
arxiv-2303-07042.creator: Raksi Kopo, Charalampos P. Bechlioulis, Kostas J. Kyriakopoulos
arxiv-2303-07042.description: Abstract This work presents a safe and efficient methodology for autonomous indoor exploration with aerial robots using Harmonic Potential Fields (HPF). The challenge of applying HPF in complex 3D environments rests on high computational load involved in solving the Laplace equation.

arxiv-2311-13640.title: Primordial Black Holes from Conformal Higgs
arxiv-2311-13640.creator: Yann Gouttenoire
arxiv-2311-13640.description: Abstract Scale-invariant extensions of the electroweak theory are not only attractive because they can dynamically generate the weak scale, but also due to their role in facilitating supercooled first-order phase transitions. We study the minimal scale-invariant U ​ ( 1 ) D U(1)_{\rm D} extension of the standard model and show that Primordial Black Holes (PBHs) can be abundantly produced.

arxiv-2402-04904.title: Predicting Interstellar Object Chemodynamics with Gaia
arxiv-2402-04904.creator: Matthew J. Hopkins, Michele T. Bannister, Chris Lintott
arxiv-2402-04904.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Matthew J. Hopkins, Michele T. Bannister, Chris Lintott. The interstellar object population of the Milky Way is a product of its stars. However, what is in fact a complex structure in the Solar neighbourhood has traditionally in ISO studies been described as smoothly distributed. Using a debiased stellar population derived from the Gaia DR3 stellar sample, we predict that the velocity distribution of ISOs is far more textured than a smooth Gaussian. The moving groups caused by Galactic resonances dominate the distribution.

arxiv-2410-09700.title: Microstructural Geometry Revealed by NMR Lineshape Analysis
arxiv-2410-09700.creator: Mohamad Niknam*, Louis-S. Bouchard
arxiv-2410-09700.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mohamad Niknam*, Louis-S. Bouchard. We introduce a technique for extracting microstructural geometry from NMR lineshape analysis in porous materials at angstrom-scale resolution with the use of weak magnetic field gradients. Diverging from the generally held view of FID signals undergoing simple exponential decay, we show that a detailed analysis of the line shape can unravel structural geometry on much smaller scales than previously thought.

arxiv-2410-20648.title: Life at low Reynolds number isn’t such a drag
arxiv-2410-20648.creator: Sujit S. Datta
arxiv-2410-20648.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sujit S. Datta. The following is an unedited version of two short articles that are forthcoming in Nature Chemical Engineering . Inspired by Purcell’s classic lecture “Life at low Reynolds number”, I discuss how scaling arguments, dimensional analysis, and fundamental concepts from chemical engineering science can be used to quantitatively describe microbial swimming—thereby helping to better understand biological systems and inspiring new engineering advances in turn. Imagine swimming in a pool on a hot summer’s day.

arxiv-2411-18501.title: Insensitizing controls for stochastic parabolic equations with dynamic boundary conditions
arxiv-2411-18501.creator: Mahmoud Baroun 1, Said Boulite 2, Abdellatif Elgrou 1, Omar Oukdach 3
arxiv-2411-18501.description: Abstract . In this paper, we establish the existence of insensitizing controls for forward linear stochastic parabolic equations with dynamic boundary conditions. We begin by reducing the insensitizing control problem to a classical controllability property of a cascade system of coupled forward-backward stochastic parabolic equations.

arxiv-2503-22250.title: Modeling Challenging Patient Interactions: LLMs for Medical Communication Training A Preprint
arxiv-2503-22250.creator: Anna Bodonhelyi, Christian Stegemann-Philipps, Alessandra Sonanini, Lea Herschbach, Marton Szep, Anne Herrmann-Werner, Teresa Festl-Wietek, Enkelejda Kasneci, Friederike Holderried
arxiv-2503-22250.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anna Bodonhelyi, Christian Stegemann-Philipps, Alessandra Sonanini, Lea Herschbach, Marton Szep, Anne Herrmann-Werner, Teresa Festl-Wietek, Enkelejda Kasneci, Friederike Holderried. Effective patient communication is pivotal in healthcare, yet traditional medical training often lacks exposure to diverse, challenging interpersonal dynamics. To bridge this gap, this study proposes the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) to simulate authentic patient communication styles, specifically the “accuser” and “rationalizer” personas derived from the Satir model, while also ensuring multilingual applicability to accommodate diverse cultural contexts and enhance accessibility for medical professionals.

arxiv-2511-14452.title: Hybrid Modeling of Photoplethysmography for Non-invasive Monitoring of Cardiovascular Parameters
arxiv-2511-14452.creator: Emanuele Palumbo, Sorawit Saengkyongam, Maria R. Cervera, Jens Behrmann, Andrew C. Miller, Guillermo Sapiro, Christina Heinze-Deml, Antoine Wehenkel
arxiv-2511-14452.description: Abstract Continuous cardiovascular monitoring can play a key role in precision health. However, some fundamental cardiac biomarkers of interest, including stroke volume and cardiac output, require invasive measurements, e.g., arterial pressure waveforms (APW). As a non-invasive alternative, photoplethysmography (PPG) measurements are routinely collected in hospital settings.

arxiv-2602-12754.title: Differential top quark cross section results from the ATLAS and CMS experiments Journal: Nuclear Physics B
arxiv-2602-12754.creator: Johannes Hessler a , b {}^{~a,b} on behalf of the ATLAS and CMS Collaborations
arxiv-2602-12754.description: Abstract This report summarizes recent results of differential top quark cross section measurements performed by the ATLAS and CMS experiments. The t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} process is studied as well as the production of single (anti-)top quarks and the interference with other Standard Model processes of the same final state. State-of-the-art theory predictions are compared to the data.

pmc-10640852.title: Role of medial prefrontal cortex and primary somatosensory cortex in self and other-directed vicarious social touch: a TMS study
pmc-10640852.creator: Ashleigh Bellard, Paula D Trotter, Francis L McGlone, Valentina Cazzato
pmc-10640852.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Conflicting evidence points to the contribution of several key nodes of the ‘social brain’ to the processing of both discriminatory and affective qualities of interpersonal touch. Whether the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), two brain areas vital for tactile mirroring and affective mentalizing, play a functional role in shared representations of C-tactile (CT) targeted affective touch is still a matter of debate.

pmc-11493297.title: The effectiveness of vitamin D supplementation in patients with end-stage knee osteoarthritis: Study protocol for a double-blinded, randomized controlled trial
pmc-11493297.creator: Qian-Wen Wang, Michael Tim-Yun Ong, Gene Chi-Wai Man, Yi-Man Yeung, Xin He, Ben Chi-Yin Choi, Jonathan Patrick Ng, Daniel Kam-Wah Mok, Tsz-Ping Lam, Patrick Shu-Hang Yung
pmc-11493297.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) knee is one of the most common chronic degenerative conditions that imposes clinical and economic burdens on individuals and societies worldwide. Previous studies showed vitamin D levels correlated positively with lean muscle mass and grip strength, implying that vitamin D supplementation may improve muscle health in knee OA subjects.

pmc-11679084.title: Exploring the Utility of the Muse Headset for Capturing the N400: Dependability and Single-Trial Analysis
pmc-11679084.creator: Hannah Begue Hayes, Cyrille Magne, Steve Ling
pmc-11679084.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Consumer-grade EEG devices, such as the InteraXon Muse 2 headband, present a promising opportunity to enhance the accessibility and inclusivity of neuroscience research. However, their effectiveness in capturing language-related ERP components, such as the N400, remains underexplored. This study thus aimed to investigate the feasibility of using the Muse 2 to measure the N400 effect in a semantic relatedness judgment task. Thirty-seven participants evaluated the semantic relatedness of word pairs while their EEG was recorded using the Muse 2.

pmc-11859149.title: Perceived mental illness stigma and self stigma among persons treated for psychotic disorders
pmc-11859149.creator: A Jambrosic Sakoman, T Jendričko, D Bošnjak Kuharić, A Tomić
pmc-11859149.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionStigma related to mental health has serious impact on persons suffering from psychiatric disorders and on their families. Self-stigma occurs when people with mental health problems internalize public attitudes, negative beliefs and stereotypes associated with psychiatric disorders.

pmc-12701083.title: Acute Kidney Failure and Myocarditis Triggered by Magic Mushroom Toxicity in a Patient With Prior Cocaine Exposure
pmc-12701083.creator: Aung Phyo Oo, Sarah Tseu, Arvind Ponnusamy
pmc-12701083.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Magic mushroom poisoning can be associated with acute kidney injury (AKI), primarily due to ischemic acute tubular necrosis (ATN). Additionally, the use of cocaine can lead to both venous and arterial thrombosis through its vasoconstrictive and prothrombotic effects. In this article, a middle-aged gentleman with a previous history of cocaine use was admitted with severe anuric AKI requiring dialysis after magic mushroom poisoning.

pmc-12742842.creator: Rama Chellappa
pmc-12742842.description: y at the University of Pennsylvania. Older adults do best when care plans see the whole person. In the first article of this issue, Shang et al. (2025) show how bringing together clinical data with everyday social factors can improve risk spotting and care planning, moving beyond diagnoses to what actually drives health for each patient.

pmc-13198543.title: PickAMoo: LIDAR-enhanced mask R-CNN segmentation for precision weight estimation in dairy cattle using smartphone imaging
pmc-13198543.creator: Oleksiy Guzhva, Emma Ternman, Mikaela Lindberg, Evgenij Telezhenko, Cecilia Kronqvist
pmc-13198543.description: Data on body weight, as well as objective measures of body condition and size, are essential for appropriate decision-making on farm level, for example in calculations of nutrient requirements, health monitoring, and breeding-related assessment. Weighing dairy cattle and assessing their body condition are labour-intensive and are therefore often not performed as frequently as desired under practical farm conditions.

pmc-13355780.title: Progressive neurological decline in a measles survivor: A case report of subacute sclerosing panencephalitis in Zambia
pmc-13355780.creator: Derby Tembo, Celia Greenlaw, Jombo Namushi, Evans Mpabalwani, Archana A. Patel, Nfwama Kawatu
pmc-13355780.description: We report a case of subacute sclerosing panencephalitis in a 14-year-old boy who presented to specialized care 17 months after the onset of symptoms, at advanced disease stage with cognitive decline, seizures, myoclonus and dystonia. A history of infantile measles, combined with characteristic electroencephalography, neuroimaging, and elevated cerebrospinal fluid measles IgG levels, confirmed the diagnosis.

pmc-13381675.title: Integrated van der Waals waveguides for all-optical nonlinear photonic circuits
pmc-13381675.creator: Xiaowen Zhang, Xiangpeng Ou, Zhican Zhou, Han Xiao, Yuxuan Huang, Chen Liu, Yujia Zhai, Xiaofeng Liu, Xixiang Zhang, Yating Wan
pmc-13381675.description: All-optical deep neural networks offer significant improvements in processing speed and energy efficiency compared with traditional electronic systems. However, achieving broadband all-optical signal transmission with ultrafast processing speed in conventional photonic waveguides remains challenging. In this work, we present an integrated photonic circuit incorporating vertically grown molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), which is also compatible with wafer-scale manufacturing.

pmc-13395410.title: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis reveals the immunosuppressive status of NK cell subpopulations in TNBC
pmc-13395410.creator: Yang Liu, Wen-Ming Cao, Ying Jin, Weizhen Xu
pmc-13395410.description: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), lacking expression of the estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), has clinical features that include high invasiveness, limited response to current immunotherapies, heightened risk of recurrence, and poorer overall prognosis.

pmc-13536411.title: Effect of antifungal therapy on salivary β-defensin 1 concentrations in patients with oral candidiasis: A pilot study
pmc-13536411.creator: Hiroyuki Hato, Taku Kimura, Noritaka Ohga, Ken-ichiro Sakata
pmc-13536411.description: obial peptide that plays a key role in the innate immune defense of the oral mucosa.1 While most defensins are induced by infection and inflammation, hBD-1 is constitutively expressed. A decrease in the expression of hBD-1 has been linked to several diseases and infections, including oral candidiasis.
